I’ve been feeling really low for a little over a year now, like this heaviness I just can’t shake. I used to be really driven with my program, but now I stare at my laptop and just…don’t start. Even reading an article feels like climbing a mountain. My mind feels slow and kind of muffled, like I’m thinking through cotton. I lose my train of thought in seminars and then feel stupid.

It’s gotten to the point where I’ve thought a lot about ending things. Not just vague thoughts—I’ve pictured specific ways I could do it, down to where it would be and how to make sure no one interrupts. That scares me, but also sometimes feels like a relief just to think about.

There’s also this other side of things that I’m embarrassed to talk about. Sometimes I’m convinced I’m meant for something huge academically, like I have a unique insight no one else has and that important people are watching my work, even though I’m barely functioning. And I hear this voice sometimes—like someone just behind me commenting on what I’m doing or saying my name—when no one is there. It doesn’t always happen when I’m at my lowest; it kind of comes and goes on its own.
D015-D007_h001.question_a:
It’s been a little over a year now that I’ve felt like this, and it just isn’t letting up. Most days I wake up with this heavy, bleak feeling, like there’s no point to anything. I used to be on top of my coursework and research, but lately I just stare at my laptop or readings and can’t make myself start. Even simple things, like doing laundry or answering emails, feel overwhelming.

My mind feels slow and foggy, like I’m moving through molasses. I reread the same paragraph over and over and it doesn’t stick. I’ve fallen behind in my program, and I barely go out or talk to classmates anymore.

Over the past few months, it’s gotten darker. I’ve been thinking a lot about ending things, not just vague thoughts—more like mapping out when I could do it so no one would find me in time, and what method would definitely work.

On top of that, I sometimes hear a man’s voice commenting on how “special” I am or how I’m meant for some big, important destiny, like I have some hidden power. I know it sounds bizarre, but in those moments it feels absolutely real. These voices and ideas only happen when I’m in this really low, depressed state—they’re not there when my mood lifts even a little.
D015-D007_h001.question_b:
It started a little over a year ago. I’ve been pretty much constantly low since then—like this heavy, gray feeling that doesn’t really lift. I used to be on top of my graduate work, but now even opening my laptop feels impossible. I miss deadlines, and I just stare at articles without taking anything in. My head feels foggy, like I’m thinking through cotton; I lose my train of thought mid-sentence in seminars.

I’ve thought a lot about ending things. Not just vague thoughts—I’ve pictured exactly how and where I’d do it, and I’ve gone over the details in my head more times than I want to admit.

On top of that, there are these…other things. For most of this year, while I’ve been depressed, I’ve also heard a man’s voice commenting on what I do, especially when I’m studying or trying to sleep. And I’ve had these strong convictions that I’m meant to be some kind of groundbreaking scientist, that I have a special role in changing the field, even though objectively my life is kind of falling apart.

What really scares me is that a couple of months ago, for about two or three weeks, my mood actually felt almost normal—I wasn’t particularly sad—but the voice and those “I’m destined for greatness” beliefs kept going just the same.

D015-D007_h004.question_both:
I’ve been feeling like this for a little over a year now. It’s not exactly being sad all the time… it’s more like everything’s muted. Stuff that used to matter – watching the match with my mates, joking with my kids – it all feels flat, like I’m just going through the motions. I mostly keep to myself now. My wife asks what’s wrong, and I just tell her I’m tired. I don’t really have the energy to talk to anyone after my shift, so I avoid family gatherings and calls.

Driving the bus, I catch myself zoning out at traffic lights, rereading the same route notes. Even at home, I’ll put the TV on and realize I’ve not followed a thing that’s happened. My mind just slips away.

Lately, I’ve had these thoughts like it’d be easier if I just didn’t wake up one morning. I’m not planning anything, but the idea of being done with all this crosses my mind a lot.

I’m also convinced there’s something seriously wrong inside my body, like my organs are rotting or poisoned, even though tests keep coming back fine. Sometimes I get this strange bitter-metallic taste in my mouth out of nowhere, like I’ve swallowed chemicals, even when I’m not eating or drinking anything. It makes me worry even more that something’s not right.
D015-D007_h004.question_a:
I’ve been feeling like this for about a year now, maybe a bit longer. It’s like someone turned the volume down on everything inside me. I’m not really sad exactly, more just blank. Things that used to matter—my kids’ school stuff, watching football, even talking with my wife—just feel…far away. I come home from my routes and mostly go straight to the bedroom. I avoid calls from friends, and at family gatherings I just sit in the corner and hope no one asks me much.

On the bus I catch myself zoning out, rereading the same schedule, losing track of what stop I’m at if I’m not careful. Even watching TV, I can’t follow the plot. A lot of nights I lie there thinking it might be easier if I just didn’t wake up, but I haven’t made any plans or anything like that.

Lately I’m convinced something is wrong inside my body—like my organs are rotting or poisoned, even though the doctor says my tests are fine. Sometimes, even when I’m not eating, I get this strong bitter-metallic taste in my mouth, like chemicals. Those weird body worries and the strange taste only started after all this low, numb feeling began, and they seem to come and go with how bad the depression is.
D015-D007_h004.question_b:
It’s been about a year now, maybe a bit more, that I’ve felt…blank. Not just sad, more like switched off inside. My wife and kids will be laughing at something on TV and I’m just sitting there, not feeling much of anything. I’ve pulled back a lot—after my shifts I just go straight to the bedroom instead of talking with them or meeting mates for a pint like I used to. Even at work, on the route, I find myself zoning out, losing track of conversations with passengers or missing turns I’ve done for years because I can’t seem to keep my mind on anything.

A lot of nights I lie there thinking it might be easier if I just didn’t wake up, not that I’m planning anything, just wishing I could disappear.

On top of that, I’m convinced there’s something seriously wrong inside my body—like my organs are rotting or poisoned—though all the tests come back normal. Sometimes, out of nowhere, I get this horrible metallic or chemical taste in my mouth, like I’ve swallowed something toxic, even when I haven’t eaten. Those tastes and the certainty something’s wrong with my insides have carried on even during a couple of stretches when my mood actually lifted for a few weeks.

D015-D007_h005.question_a:
It’s been about a year now, maybe a bit more, that I’ve just… gone downhill. I cry all the time, for no real reason. I’ll be in the workshop, sanding a piece of walnut, and suddenly I’m just standing there with tears running down my face. I used to love what I do—picking out grains, designing custom pieces—but now I can’t bring myself to care. Orders are late, I avoid clients, and my ex has started taking our daughter more because I can’t keep up.

My head feels thick, like I’m wading through mud. Simple measurements or invoices feel confusing; I reread things over and over and still can’t think straight. Sometimes when I’m driving over a bridge or near a busy road, I get these strong urges to just turn the wheel or step into traffic. I haven’t made any plans, but the pull is there and it scares me.

On top of that, when I’m at my lowest, I’m convinced something catastrophic is coming—that the world is basically over already, just rotting from the inside out. Around those times I’ll suddenly taste this bitter, metallic flavor in my mouth, like blood or chemicals, even when I’m not eating anything. Those beliefs and weird tastes only show up when I’m in this deep dark place; when my mood briefly lifts a bit, they fade with it.

My head feels stuffed with cotton; I stare at measurements and can’t keep numbers straight. It’s like trying to think through fog.

There are times when I get this sudden urge to just step into traffic or jump off the pedestrian bridge near my shop. It hits hard and fast, like an impulse, even when I don’t have a specific plan—I just feel like disappearing.

On top of that, I’m convinced something terrible is coming, like the world is winding down, rotting from the inside. It doesn’t feel like a worry; it feels like a fact.
